description: The graph illustrates the loss trends for two experimental setups, Ex1 and Ex2, during continual pretraining, with separate lines for training and validation losses. The x-axis, labeled "Step," is linear and ranges from 0 to 600,000, with major tick marks at intervals of 100,000. The y-axis, labeled "Loss," uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from $2 \times 10^0$ (2) to $1.2 \times 10^1$ (12), with labeled ticks at $2 \times 10^0$, $3 \times 10^0$, $4 \times 10^0$, $6 \times 10^0$, $10^1$, $1.1 \times 10^1$, and $1.2 \times 10^1$. The legend identifies four distinct lines: "Ex1 Loss" (solid blue line with blue circular markers), "Ex2 Loss" (solid teal line with teal circular markers), "Ex1 Validation Loss" (dashed blue line with blue circular markers), and "Ex2 Validation Loss" (dashed teal line with teal circular markers). The "Ex1 Loss" line starts at a loss of approximately 3.7 at step 0 and rapidly decreases to a stable value of around 1.9 by step 100,000. The "Ex2 Loss" line begins at a higher loss of about 11.5 and also decreases sharply, stabilizing around 2.1 by step 200,000. Both "Ex1 Validation Loss" and "Ex2 Validation Loss" lines follow a similar pattern, starting at approximately 5.0 and 4.8 respectively, and decreasing to stable values of around 3.1 and 3.2 respectively, remaining relatively flat for the remainder of the training. The "Ex2 Validation Loss" line is consistently above the "Ex1 Validation Loss" line throughout the training process.
